terms.en: eai in vedeai (you used to see)

en.title: eai in vedeai (you used to see)
en.summary: This item illustrates the Romanian diphthong eai as found in the verb form vedeai.

sections.title: The sound of eai
paragraphs: The letters eai sound like /e̯aj/. You hear this group in the word (vedeai) /veˈde̯aj/, which means you were seeing. These letters make only one combined sound in Romanian. You say all three vowels together in one single breath.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: Start with your tongue mid high and glide quickly. Open your mouth wide for the main vowel sound. Then raise your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Your lips stay spread throughout the glide. Your voice vibrates across the whole flow. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the steady vibration.

sections.title: When it appears
paragraphs: The letters eai appear in stressed syllables. They always make the sound /e̯aj/. You find them at the end of past tense verbs, like in (spuneai) /spuˈne̯aj/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not split these letters into three separate syllables. English words like eye or aye start directly on an open vowel. Glide smoothly from a brief front vowel instead. Keep the entire sequence within one syllable.
